candidates.source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (Obchodní rejstřík, Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory commercial register plus the Sbírka listin document vault where every CZ s.r.o./a.s. must file annual accounts (účetní závěrka), annual reports (výroční zpráva), auditor reports, articles, merger projects and reports on relations between related parties (zpráva o vztazích). For payment vendors and PSPs this is the primary evidence of revenue, revenue concentration, named key customers, group structure and M&A that marketing never discloses.
candidates.access_status: public, free, no login; PDF/scan documents
candidates.legal_status: public register established by law (zák. 304/2013 Sb. o veřejných rejstřících)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve target companies to IČO via ARES, then fetch the Sbírka listin listing per subject-id and download filed PDFs; OCR scanned annual reports; schedule re-checks after the 30 Jun / 31 Dec filing peaks. Throttle politely; prefer dataor.justice.cz bulk for structured fields.
queries_used: justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva platební instituce s.r.o.

candidates.source_name: Veřejné rejstříky – nový portál Ministerstva spravedlnosti (verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Successor/parallel front-end to or.justice.cz with rozšířené vyhledávání (advanced search) allowing screening by predmet podnikání, address, statutory persons — enables building a population of CZ payment/IT vendors rather than looking up one known name at a time.
candidates.access_status: public, free
candidates.legal_status: state-operated public register
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use rozšířené vyhledávání to enumerate candidate entities by activity/address, export IČO list, then join to ARES + Sbírka listin.
queries_used: evidence skutečných majitelů esm.justice.cz vyhledávání veřejný přístup

candidates.source_name: OpenData ISVR – dataor.justice.cz (bulk open data of the Czech public registers)
candidates.why_relevant: Full-scope bulk XML/CSV dumps of the public registers (since April 2019) — the machine-readable backbone for building a persistent actor map of CZ payment vendors, their statutory bodies, shareholders, capital and address history without scraping the HTML register.
candidates.source_subtype: open data bulk dump / register export
candidates.access_status: public open data, free download, annual/periodic datasets
candidates.legal_status: open data under nařízení vlády 425/2016 Sb.; open re-use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled bulk download of yearly XML/CSV packages into a local warehouse; diff successive vintages to detect ownership/statutory-body changes. Contact point dataor@msp.justice.cz. Note documented limitation: no name history and no birth dates of officers.
queries_used: dataor.justice.cz open data obchodní rejstřík XML full dataset download

candidates.source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (Ministerstvo financí ČR)
candidates.why_relevant: Master resolver for CZ legal entities: IČO, legal form, NACE/CZ-NACE activity codes (e.g. 6419, 6499, 6612, 6209), registered address, register linkages. The canonical entity-resolution layer that makes every other filing source joinable, and the way to enumerate firms by payment-related NACE codes.
candidates.source_subtype: administrative entity register + REST API + open data
candidates.access_status: public, free, documented REST API and open-data dumps
candidates.legal_status: state register; open data; documented usage conditions
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the documented ARES REST API for lookup and NACE-based enumeration; respect the stated fair-use limit (MF reserves the right to restrict users exceeding ~500 queries/minute or automating random-data crawls). Prefer the MF open-data bulk dataset for large joins.
queries_used: ares.gov.cz vyhledávání ekonomických subjektů API otevřená data
ares.gov.cz vyhledávání společnost platební služby CZ-NACE 6419

candidates.source_name: Evidence skutečných majitelů (ESM) – beneficial ownership register
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory beneficial-ownership register — the only authoritative way to unmask who really stands behind a CZ fintech/PSP behind layered holdings. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the public part was made inaccessible by the Ministry of Justice on 17 December 2025 following CJEU/NSS case law; access now requires data-box self-access, privileged public-authority access, AML-obliged-person request, or proving legitimate interest to a court.
candidates.access_status: public part closed since 2025-12-17; restricted access only
candidates.legal_status: statutory register; public access withdrawn on privacy/CJEU grounds — do not attempt to circumvent
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Do not scrape. Use only (a) historical extracts already lawfully obtained, (b) ownership inferred from Sbírka listin filings and register shareholder entries, (c) formal request routes if the organisation qualifies as an AML-obliged person.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball to MSp and FAU notices
queries_used: evidence skutečných majitelů esm.justice.cz vyhledávání veřejný přístup
obchodní rejstřík skutečný majitel fintech společnost Česko
candidates.observed_blocker: Public section of ESM closed to the public from 17 Dec 2025 per Ministry of Justice notice; only privileged/AML/legitimate-interest access remains

candidates.source_name: ČNB JERRS – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative licence-status layer: which entities hold platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, PSMR (poskytovatel platebních služeb malého rozsahu) or e-money issuer permissions, plus passporting notifications. Pairs with justice.cz filings to separate genuinely licensed PSPs from resellers/agents, and to build the competitor universe before pulling accounts.
candidates.source_subtype: supervisory register / licence list with web services
candidates.access_status: public, free; WS JERRS web services available since 1 Jul 2019
candidates.legal_status: official supervisory register
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query WS JERRS web services for the payment-institution / e-money / PSMR lists on a monthly cadence, diff for new entrants, licence withdrawals and name changes; join to IČO for the justice.cz filing pull.
queries_used: ČNB seznam regulovaných subjektů platební instituce registr JERRS

candidates.source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) – smlouvy.gov.cz
candidates.why_relevant: Mandatory publication of contracts above CZK 50,000 by state-owned and public entities — for banking/payments this exposes real supplier relationships and contract values with state-linked banks and public bodies (ČNB, ministries, state agencies, Česká pošta / Poštovní spořitelna ecosystem, ČEB/EGAP). Hard evidence of vendor wins that marketing case studies only hint at.
candidates.source_subtype: statutory contract register with open-data API
candidates.access_status: public, free, no registration; XLSX export and bulk metadata dumps
candidates.legal_status: statutory register under zák. 340/2015 Sb.; metadata are open data (dataset contains personal data — GDPR care required)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Consume the ISRS application interface / monthly metadata dumps; filter by supplier IČO for the vendor watchlist and by keyword (platební terminál, bankomat, ATM, karetní, core banking) in subject lines; minimise personal data on ingest.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles category inference (who must publish) + local-language search
queries_used: registr smluv smlouvy.gov.cz API otevřená data banka dodavatel smlouva

candidates.source_name: Insolvenční rejstřík (ISIR) – eisir.justice.cz
candidates.why_relevant: Distress signal on vendors, resellers and fintech competitors: insolvency petitions, creditor filings and full case files since 2008. Creditor lists in an insolvency file are also an indirect customer/supplier map of a failing payments firm.
candidates.source_subtype: court register / case-file archive with web services
candidates.access_status: public, free; ISIR_WS XML web service and monitoring service available
candidates.legal_status: public register under zák. 182/2006 Sb.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register the vendor watchlist IČOs with the ISIR monitoring web service (SLEDOVANIWS) for automatic alerts; pull XML case data via ISIR_WS.
queries_used: isir.justice.cz insolvenční rejstřík vyhledávání otevřená data

candidates.source_name: Obchodní věstník (ov.gov.cz) – official Czech commercial gazette
candidates.why_relevant: Official gazette carrying statutory notices: liquidations, capital changes, general-meeting convocations and (historically) transformation/merger notices. Useful as a time-stamped event feed on CZ payment vendors. Note: the 2024 amendment to the transformations act removed several mandatory OV publications, shifting merger projects into the Sbírka listin instead — so coverage of M&A events has partly migrated.
candidates.access_status: public web search of entries; older archive also mirrored at ov.ihned.cz
candidates.legal_status: official state gazette
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword/IČO monitoring of new entries; cross-check merger events against Sbírka listin projekt přeměny filings since the publication duty moved there.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on merger publication duty
queries_used: Obchodní věstník ov.justice.cz přeměny fúze projekt přeměny zveřejnění

candidates.source_name: CRIBIS (CRIF – Czech Credit Bureau) company profiles
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial credit-bureau layer over the statutory registers: financial ratios, payment morale/REPI index, ownership graphs, links to Centrální evidence exekucí and cadastre. Fastest route to a comparable financial scorecard across a set of CZ payment vendors when raw Sbírka listin PDFs are too slow.
candidates.access_status: paid subscription; limited free teaser data
candidates.legal_status: proprietary commercial database — licence terms apply; bulk scraping not permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Licensed access with manual/API export under contract; use for targeted profiles rather than mass harvesting. Never redistribute raw records.
queries_used: merk.cz cribis.cz rejstrik-firem.kurzy.cz profil firmy účetní závěrka platební služby

candidates.source_name: Rejstřík firem Kurzy.cz (rejstrik-firem.kurzy.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Free aggregator of justice.cz data with pre-computed ownership/officer relationship graphs and a browsable Sbírka listin mirror — very efficient for snowballing from one payments vendor to its directors, sister companies and shared shareholders.
candidates.access_status: public, free (ad-supported)
candidates.legal_status: third-party republication of public register data; site ToS apply
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-rate fetching for snowballing officer and shareholder links; always re-verify any material fact against or.justice.cz before use as evidence.
queries_used: merk.cz cribis.cz rejstrik-firem.kurzy.cz profil firmy účetní závěrka platební služby

candidates.source_name: Rejstřík firem Peníze.cz
candidates.why_relevant: Second free mirror/aggregator of the commercial register with company profiles, officer histories and financial summaries; useful as a cross-check when one aggregator's parsing of a filing is ambiguous.
candidates.access_status: public, free
candidates.legal_status: third-party republication of public data; ToS apply
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Spot-check lookups only; not a bulk source.
queries_used: merk.cz cribis.cz rejstrik-firem.kurzy.cz profil firmy účetní závěrka platební služby

candidates.source_name: Chytrý rejstřík (chytryrejstrik.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Aggregator adding derived signals — estimated revenue (tržby), risk flags, vehicle fleets, contacts — on top of register data; a cheap proxy scale indicator for small CZ payment vendors that file abbreviated accounts.
candidates.access_status: public with freemium tiers
candidates.legal_status: commercial site; ToS apply; derived figures are estimates not filings
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual lookups; treat derived revenue as an estimate, always label as non-statutory.
queries_used: justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva platební instituce s.r.o.

candidates.source_name: European e-Justice Portal – Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS)
candidates.why_relevant: Single EU entry point (live since June 2017) into all Member State business registers plus Iceland/Liechtenstein/Norway, with EUID identifiers, cross-border branch and cross-border merger notifications. The route from a CZ subsidiary of a payments vendor to its foreign parent's home register — and vice versa. Note it exposes only basic harmonised data, not filings or financials.
candidates.access_status: public, free; searches run in real time against national registers
candidates.legal_status: official EU portal
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use interactively to map parent/branch chains and obtain EUIDs, then go to the relevant national register for the actual filings.
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search on cross-border register interconnection
queries_used: BRIS e-justice business registers search interconnection company information EU

candidates.source_name: GLEIF – Global LEI Index
candidates.why_relevant: Free bulk LEI reference data including Level-2 'who owns whom' direct and ultimate parent relationships. For CZ banks, PSPs and payment institutions with an LEI, this gives a machine-readable group-structure skeleton to validate against register filings, and a stable cross-border identifier joining CZ IČO to foreign parents.
candidates.access_status: public, free bulk files and API
candidates.legal_status: open reference data (CC0-style terms per GLEIF)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the concatenated LEI-CDF and RR-CDF files monthly; filter legal jurisdiction CZ; join on registration authority entity id (IČO).
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles inference (who assigns cross-border identifiers) plus LEI hit in register search results
queries_used: justice.cz sbírka listin výroční zpráva platební instituce s.r.o.

candidates.source_name: UK Companies House – filings of foreign parents of CZ payments vendors
candidates.why_relevant: Many payment vendors, acquirers and fintechs active in CZ are UK-parented or have UK holding entities; UK group accounts frequently disclose segment revenue, CEE subsidiary lists and acquisitions in far more detail than the Czech subsidiary's abbreviated accounts. Free full-text filing search plus a public REST API.
candidates.access_status: public, free, registered API key for the REST API
candidates.legal_status: official register; open re-use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Companies House REST API + advanced/full-text search for the parent names identified via BRIS/LEI; pull group accounts PDFs and extract subsidiary lists.
queries_used: annual accounts Czech subsidiary payments vendor revenue customers

candidates.source_name: Bundesanzeiger / Unternehmensregister (Germany) – parent and DACH group filings
candidates.why_relevant: German-parented payment/banking technology groups (and Austrian/DACH holding structures serving CZ) publish Jahresabschluss and Konzernabschluss with subsidiary lists (Anteilsbesitzliste) naming their Czech entities — evidence of group ownership and CEE segment performance not visible in CZ filings.
candidates.access_status: public search, free for most filings; some documents chargeable; session/anti-bot behaviour likely
candidates.legal_status: official register
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted manual retrieval for named parents; expect session-based navigation that resists naive scraping — record as unverified rather than dead if a fetch fails.
queries_used: annual accounts Czech subsidiary payments vendor revenue customers
candidates.observed_blocker: not fetched in this pass; portal is known to be session-driven

candidates.source_name: SEC EDGAR – US-listed payments/banking-technology vendors
candidates.why_relevant: Global ATM/POS and core-banking vendors competing in CZ that are US-listed file 10-K/20-F with segment revenue, EMEA commentary, customer-concentration disclosures, risk factors and subsidiary exhibits (Ex-21) naming Czech entities — the richest free competitor-economics evidence available for that tier of the market.
candidates.source_subtype: securities regulator filing archive with full-text search and API
candidates.access_status: public, free; EDGAR full-text search and JSON APIs (declared User-Agent required)
candidates.legal_status: public government filings; open re-use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: EDGAR full-text search for 'Czech' / 'Czechia' within the vendor watchlist CIKs; harvest Ex-21 subsidiary lists and segment notes; set a compliant User-Agent header per SEC policy.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles inference (who must disclose to investors)
queries_used: annual accounts Czech subsidiary payments vendor revenue customers

candidates.source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek / NEN – Czech public procurement records
candidates.why_relevant: Award notices from state-linked banks and public bodies disclose winning payment/IT vendors, contract values and durations — a statutory-disclosure complement that dates and prices vendor-customer relationships, and reveals losing bidders (i.e. the real competitive set).
candidates.access_status: public, free search; open-data exports available
candidates.legal_status: statutory publication under zák. 134/2016 Sb.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled export/monitoring filtered by CPV codes for payment terminals, ATMs and banking software, and by contracting authority; cross-check with TED for EU-level notices.
queries_used: registr smluv smlouvy.gov.cz API otevřená data banka dodavatel smlouva

candidates.source_name: MF ČR open data portal (data.mf.gov.cz) and national open data catalogue (data.gov.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Master catalogue of every CZ state dataset, including ARES, Registr smluv and register exports — the systematic way to discover further statutory-disclosure datasets relevant to payments vendors rather than guessing portal URLs.
candidates.access_status: public, free; SPARQL and API access
candidates.legal_status: open data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyword sweep of the catalogue (rejstřík, subjekt, smlouva, finanční trh) to detect newly published datasets; register the distribution URLs in the source registry.
queries_used: ares.gov.cz vyhledávání ekonomických subjektů API otevřená data

negative_findings.description: The public part of the Czech beneficial ownership register (Evidence skutečných majitelů, esm.justice.cz) was made inaccessible to the public by the Ministry of Justice effective 17 December 2025, citing Supreme Court, Supreme Administrative Court and CJEU case law on disproportionate interference with privacy.
negative_findings.result_summary: ESM can no longer be used as an open ownership-unmasking source; access is limited to the entity itself via data box, privileged public authorities, AML-obliged persons on request, or parties proving legitimate interest to a court.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This removes the single most direct route to identifying who really stands behind a CZ fintech or PSP; ownership analysis must fall back on shareholder entries in the obchodní rejstřík, Sbírka listin filings, LEI Level-2 parent data and foreign parent registers, all of which are less complete.

negative_findings.description: The 2024 amendment to the Czech transformations act removed the duty to publish paid notices about merger/transformation projects and creditor notices in the Obchodní věstník; the projekt přeměny and creditor notices are now deposited in the Sbírka listin at least one month before approval.
negative_findings.result_summary: M&A event detection has shifted from a searchable gazette feed to per-company document filings.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A monitoring pipeline built only on Obchodní věstník will silently miss vendor mergers and acquisitions from 2024 onward; watchlist-driven Sbírka listin polling is now required.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, publicly documented open-data dataset was found that extracts structured financial statement line items (revenue, EBITDA) from Sbírka listin PDFs for CZ companies; filings appear to be published as documents (often scans) rather than as structured XBRL-style data.
negative_findings.result_summary: Financial extraction from Czech statutory filings requires document download plus OCR/parsing, or a paid credit-bureau layer (CRIBIS, Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet-type providers).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cost and latency of the workstream's financial-evidence pipeline are materially higher than in jurisdictions with structured filing data; budget for OCR or a commercial licence.

negative_findings.description: Both ARES and the credit-bureau aggregators impose usage limits or licence conditions: MF ČR reserves the right to restrict users exceeding roughly 500 queries per minute or performing random-data automated crawling of ARES, and CRIBIS-type services are contractual databases that forbid bulk extraction.
negative_findings.result_summary: Automated collection must be rate-limited and, for commercial profiles, licence-based rather than scraped.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ignoring these terms risks IP blocks on the single most important entity-resolution service for the whole CZ workstream.

negative_findings.description: German Unternehmensregister/Bundesanzeiger and some ČNB JERRS application endpoints were not fetched in this pass; their URLs are recorded from search results and prior knowledge, not from a successful retrieval.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as unverified rather than dead; liveness is to be established by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false 'dead source' records for portals that are typically session-driven or bot-defended.

coverage_gaps.description: This pass mapped the register infrastructure but did not yet materialise the actual watchlist of CZ payment institutions, e-money institutions, PSMR providers and banking-technology vendors with their IČO identifiers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one enumeration pass: pull the ČNB JERRS payment-institution/e-money/PSMR lists and an ARES NACE-based sweep (6419, 6492, 6499, 6612, 6619, 6209, 6201, 4741, 2620), reconcile to IČO, and store as the canonical CZ actor map that drives all Sbírka listin polling.

coverage_gaps.description: With ESM closed to the public, there is no confirmed replacement for beneficial-ownership evidence on privately held CZ fintechs whose shareholder of record is an opaque holding company.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess whether the organisation qualifies as an AML-obliged person able to request ESM extracts; otherwise build a triangulation method from register shareholder entries, notarial deeds in the Sbírka listin, GLEIF Level-2 data, foreign parent registers and OpenCorporates-style aggregators, and document the residual uncertainty explicitly.

coverage_gaps.description: Paid pan-European filing aggregators (Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet CZ, Orbis/Bureau van Dijk, OpenCorporates) were inferred from first principles but not searched or priced in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated commercial-aggregator scan and compare CZ filing coverage, subsidiary-tree depth and licence terms against CRIBIS before committing to a paid layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Many CZ payment vendors operate as CZ/SK pairs; the Slovak counterpart registers (ORSR, RPVS register of public sector partners, Finstat) were out of the stated CZ scope but are essential to see the full group.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: If scope is ever widened, add ORSR/RPVS/Finstat as a sibling cell; meanwhile flag CZ entities whose parent is Slovak so the gap is visible in downstream analysis.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Czech statutory filings is thin: the register front-ends offer partial English UI but filed documents (výroční zpráva, zpráva o vztazích) are essentially Czech-only, sometimes as scans.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for Czech-language OCR and machine translation in the extraction stage; do not assume any English filing exists for CZ-domiciled vendors.

brief: The Czech statutory-disclosure layer is unusually strong for competitive intelligence on payments vendors: or.justice.cz plus its Sbírka listin holds mandatory annual reports, audited accounts, merger projects and related-party reports, and dataor.justice.cz republishes the whole register as bulk open data, while ARES supplies free entity resolution and NACE-based enumeration and ČNB JERRS supplies the licence layer that separates real payment institutions from resellers. Around this core sit high-value complements that date and price vendor-customer relationships — Registr smluv, the procurement gazette/NEN, Obchodní věstník and ISIR — plus commercial and free aggregators (CRIBIS, Kurzy.cz, Peníze.cz, Chytrý rejstřík) that shortcut PDF parsing at the cost of authority. The one serious regression is beneficial ownership: the public part of the ESM register was closed on 17 December 2025, so unmasking who stands behind a CZ fintech now depends on triangulating register shareholder entries, GLEIF Level-2 parent data and foreign parent filings via BRIS, UK Companies House, Bundesanzeiger and SEC EDGAR. Filings are Czech-language documents rather than structured data, so the practical bottleneck for this cell is OCR and extraction, not source availability.
